problem: The text prints "210 = 1024". A student reads this as the number two hundred ten, which equals 1024 is false. The intent is 2 to the power 10.
fix: A 0–5 V signal into a 10-bit ADC gives 2¹⁰ = 1024 codes.

problem: The wording "the microcontroller sets sleep current if it is not put into deep sleep" is garbled and can be read two ways; the reader cannot tell which state is being described.
fix: The radio sets the peak current. The sleep current is set mainly by the microcontroller when it is not put into its deep-sleep mode, plus any leakage in the regulator and the sensor left powered.

problem: The lead says a sensor node is "the hardware form of this idea" (the smart object), but Section 1 says a sensor node only senses and forwards, while a smart object also adds actuation and identity. The two statements contradict each other.
fix: A sensor node, also called a mote, is the hardware core of this idea: it supplies sensing, computing, communication and power. Add actuation and identity and the node becomes a full smart object.

problem: The figure places an Identification block inside the sensor node, but Section 2 lists only four units for a node (sensing, processing, transceiver, power) and Section 1 says identity is what a smart object adds on top of a mote. The figure contradicts the text.
fix: Either retitle the figure "Inside a smart object" and keep the Identification block, or drop the Identification block from the sensor-node figure and show it only in the smart-object picture.
